code: # Attach detfield, and ggplot2 for the figures library(detfield) library(ggplot2) # Find a file included with the package in_file <- function(name) system.file("extdata", name, package = "detfield") serial_text <- c(receiver_serial = "character") # Read the three range-test files and count their rows rt_detections <- read.csv(in_file("stoney_range_test_detections.csv"),                           colClasses = serial_text) rt_receivers <- read.csv(in_file("stoney_range_test_receivers.csv"),                          colClasses = serial_text) rt_tags <- read.csv(in_file("stoney_range_test_tags.csv")) c(detections = nrow(rt_detections), receivers = nrow(rt_receivers),   tags = nrow(rt_tags)) #> detections  receivers       tags  #>      14281          6         10 # Convert detection, deployment and recovery times to UTC date-times rt_detections$datetime <- as.POSIXct(rt_detections$datetime, tz = "UTC") for (col in c("deploy_datetime", "recover_datetime")) {   rt_receivers[[col]] <- as.POSIXct(rt_receivers[[col]], tz = "UTC")   rt_tags[[col]] <- as.POSIXct(rt_tags[[col]], tz = "UTC") } range(rt_detections$datetime) #> [1] "2024-05-19 23:50:01 UTC" "2024-05-25 00:09:54 UTC" # Count transmissions sent and heard per receiver, tag and hour range_test <- range_test_counts(rt_detections, rt_receivers, rt_tags) #> 121 of 14,281 detections are not counted: other transmitters or #>   receivers, or bins a deployment covers only in part. #> 2 of 1,440 rows had more detections than the delay allows #>   transmissions; `sent` was raised to the count in those rows. head(range_test[, c("datetime", "depth_m", "distance_m", "sent", "heard")]) #>     datetime depth_m distance_m sent heard #> 1 2024-05-20       1        150   24    17 #> 2 2024-05-20       1        350   24     9 #> 3 2024-05-20       1        650   24     1 #> 4 2024-05-20       1       1100   24     0 #> 5 2024-05-20       1       1600   24     0 #> 6 2024-05-20       1        300   24     6 # Count the rows per receiver depth (m) and distance (m) table(range_test$depth_m, range_test$distance_m) #>      #>      100 150 200 250 300 350 550 650 700 750 1100 1150 1600 #>   1   48  48  96  48  48  48  48  96  48  48   48   48   48 #>   25  48  48  96  48  48  48  48  96  48  48   48   48   48

code: # Fit a binomial GLM of heard out of sent on distance and receiver depth fit <- glm(cbind(heard, sent - heard) ~ distance_m * depth_m,            family = binomial, data = range_test) # Compute the Pearson dispersion: near 1 means no spread beyond the binomial dispersion <- sum(residuals(fit, type = "pearson")^2) / df.residual(fit) dispersion #> [1] 0.861846 # Wrap the fitted model with a spread of 0 model <- de_model(fit, sigma = list(station_hour = 0)) model #> <de_model> glm, cbind(heard, sent - heard) ~ distance_m * depth_m #>   reads: distance_m, depth_m  #>   sigma: station_hour 0 logits #>   blocked line of sight: curve read at the distance through water # Predict the fitted curve every 10 m at the two tested depths curves <- expand.grid(distance_m = seq(0, 1600, by = 10), depth_m = c(1, 25)) curves$p <- plogis(model$predict(curves$distance_m, depth_m = curves$depth_m)) # Pool the share heard at each depth and distance over hours pooled <- aggregate(cbind(heard, sent) ~ depth_m + distance_m,                     data = range_test, FUN = sum) # Plot the curves over the pooled shares ggplot(curves, aes(distance_m, p, colour = factor(depth_m))) +   geom_line(linewidth = 1) +   geom_point(data = pooled, aes(y = heard / sent), shape = 21,              fill = "white", size = 2.4, stroke = 1) +   scale_colour_viridis_d(name = "Receiver depth (m)", end = 0.7) +   scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1)) +   labs(x = "Distance (m)", y = "Detection probability per transmission") +   theme_positionr()

code: # Average the hourly surfaces per cell over all detected hours use <- aggregate(list(share = surface$prob), by = list(cell = surface$cell),                  FUN = sum) use$share <- use$share / nrow(hours) # Share of the true minutes of the detected hours in each cell true_use <- aggregate(list(share = minutes$cell),                       by = list(cell = minutes$cell), FUN = length) true_use$share <- true_use$share / nrow(minutes) # Measure the overlap of the two: 1 when identical, 0 when disjoint both <- merge(use, true_use, by = "cell", all = TRUE,               suffixes = c("_estimated", "_true")) both[is.na(both)] <- 0 overlap <- sum(pmin(both$share_estimated, both$share_true)) round(overlap, 2) #> [1] 0.5 # Distance from every cell to the nearest cell the animals swam through visited <- terra::rast(lake) visited[unique(minutes$cell)] <- 1 to_track <- terra::values(terra::distance(visited), mat = FALSE) # Share of the use map within 200 m, and in the cells swum through near_track <- c(within_200_m = sum(use$share[to_track[use$cell] <= 200]),                 same_cell = sum(use$share[to_track[use$cell] == 0])) round(near_track, 2) #> within_200_m    same_cell  #>         0.99         0.91 # Keep, per map, the smallest set of cells holding 95% of its total top_95 <- function(map) {   map <- map[order(-map$share), ]   map[cumsum(map$share) - map$share < 0.95 * sum(map$share), ] } use_95 <- top_95(use) true_use_95 <- top_95(true_use) c(estimated_cells = nrow(use_95), of = nrow(use),   true_cells = nrow(true_use_95), of = nrow(true_use)) #> estimated_cells              of      true_cells              of  #>             913            1999            1253            1604 # Stack the two maps as panels, each cell with its coordinates panel_names <- c("(a) Estimated: mean of the hourly surfaces",                  "(b) True: minutes of the detected hours") use_cells <- rbind(data.frame(use_95, panel = panel_names[1]),                    data.frame(true_use_95, panel = panel_names[2])) use_cells <- cbind(use_cells, round(terra::xyFromCell(lake, use_cells$cell), 1)) # Give every water cell a row in both panels, empty where it has no share use_cells <- merge(merge(water, data.frame(panel = panel_names), by = NULL),                    use_cells, all.x = TRUE) use_cells$panel <- factor(use_cells$panel, panel_names) # Map water in grey, then the shares on one magma scale for both panels ggplot(use_cells, aes(x, y)) +   geom_raster(aes(fill = share)) +   scale_fill_viridis_c(name = "Share of\nanimal-hours\nper cell",                        option = "magma", trans = "sqrt", na.value = "grey88") +   layer_receivers(receivers, size = 1.2, stroke = 0.45) +   facet_wrap(~panel, ncol = 1) +   coord_equal() +   labs(x = "Easting (m, UTM 17N)", y = "Northing (m, UTM 17N)") +   annotation_scale_bar(location = "br") +   theme_positionr() # Split each drawn cell's probability by whether its hour had one receiver cell_mass <- data.frame(animal_id = surface$animal_id,                         bin_start = surface$bin_start, cell = surface$cell,                         prob = surface$prob) cell_mass <- merge(cell_mass[cell_mass$cell %in% use_95$cell, ],                    hours[c("animal_id", "bin_start", "receivers_heard")]) cell_mass$single_prob <- cell_mass$prob * (cell_mass$receivers_heard == 1) by_cell <- aggregate(cbind(prob, single_prob) ~ cell, data = cell_mass,                      FUN = sum) # code: # Stoney Lake: a detection field from distances through water, the # detections counted per hour, and one surface per detected hour. tif <- system.file("extdata", "stoney_depth.tif", package = "detfield") grid <- terra::rast(tif) # Beyond 2 km the Stoney curve is below 0.001 at every receiver; leaving # those pairs out keeps the example quick. dist <- water_distances(grid, stoney_track$receivers,                         max_distance = 2000) model <- de_logistic(d50 = c(250, 750), d05 = c(500, 1500), depth = c(1, 35)) field <- de_field(dist, de_model(model, sigma = list(station_hour = 0))) #> 194 of 7,669 receiver-cell pairs with p >= 0.05 have land on the #>   straight line between them; with blocked = 0 the curve is read on #>   them as if the line were clear. See `blocked` in ?de_model. counts <- bin_detections(stoney_track$detections, stoney_track$receivers,                          stoney_track$tags) surface <- location_surface(counts, field) surface #> Location surface: 5 animals, 212 bins, 5,934 cells kept in all #> Cells kept per bin: median 19 of 4,818 water cells (range 6 to 220) #> Likelihood: binomial (detections and misses at every listening #>   receiver) #> Spread: none (overdispersion = "none") #> Each bin keeps the smallest set of cells holding 0.999 of its #>   probability #> Misfit: 10 of 212 bins have a detecting receiver whose count the #>   surface gives a chance below 0.01 #> Near: 47 of 212 bins put under 0.001 of their probability within 223.6 #>   to 447.2 m of the receiver with the most detections (per receiver, #>   its farthest cell centre at p >= 0.5) #> Modes sit a median 316 m (max 707 m) from the nearest detecting #>   receiver, over 212 bins #>   animal_id           bin_start cell       prob #> 1 stoney-01 2024-06-01 04:00:00 2502 0.11482306 #> 2 stoney-01 2024-06-01 04:00:00 2836 0.11203616 #> 3 stoney-01 2024-06-01 04:00:00 2669 0.10675649 #> 4 stoney-01 2024-06-01 04:00:00 2670 0.08254470 #> 5 stoney-01 2024-06-01 04:00:00 2837 0.08173242 #> 6 stoney-01 2024-06-01 04:00:00 2334 0.07061498 bins <- attr(surface, "bins") head(bins[, c("animal_id", "bin_start", "n_cells", "misfit_p", "mode_dist_m")]) #>   animal_id           bin_start n_cells     misfit_p mode_dist_m #> 1 stoney-01 2024-06-01 04:00:00      38 0.5264966814    447.2136 #> 2 stoney-01 2024-06-01 05:00:00       8 0.3541473904    282.8427 #> 3 stoney-01 2024-06-01 06:00:00       9 0.3277769506    424.2641 #> 4 stoney-01 2024-06-01 07:00:00      12 0.3660876826    223.6068 #> 5 stoney-01 2024-06-01 08:00:00       9 0.0001923432    316.2278 #> 6 stoney-01 2024-06-01 09:00:00      32 0.5585926296    360.5551

code: tif <- system.file("extdata", "stoney_depth.tif", package = "detfield") grid <- terra::rast(tif) # Beyond 2 km the Stoney curve is below 0.001 at every receiver; leaving # those pairs out keeps the example quick. dist <- water_distances(grid, stoney_track$receivers, max_distance = 2000) model <- de_logistic(d50 = c(250, 750), d05 = c(500, 1500), depth = c(1, 35)) field <- de_field(dist, de_model(model, sigma = list(station_hour = 0))) #> 194 of 7,669 receiver-cell pairs with p >= 0.05 have land on the #>   straight line between them; with blocked = 0 the curve is read on #>   them as if the line were clear.
